fields.Name: ORD-17 - Returns
fields.Description: Money going BACK, which is the direction almost nothing was designed for (RT1-RT12). Every other bundle sells something; the reverse path shares the same confirm code, and that sharing is what makes it worth testing separately - the forward path's assumptions are invisible until a negative number runs through them. Three matter enough to pin: a reversal is the MIRROR of an entry (sides swapped, amounts positive) and never a negation, because accounting rejects negative amounts outright so a naive -amount does not fail a balance check, it fails to post at all; a reversal unwinds a purchase so it must not re-trigger what a purchase triggers, since materializing a subscription on a reversal creates a second subscription every time one is cancelled; and tax and discounts reverse WITH the line, because a return that keeps the tax overcharges the customer while one that reverses list price refunds money never paid. The recurring shape is that a wrong reversal still balances, so these checks assert what the entry is made OF.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: A negative quantity with no origin line is refused with a message naming ReversesOrderLineID; the same line with an origin books, proving the guard is about provenance rather than sign; the reversal debits exactly what the sale credited on the same set of accounts with every amount positive; a partial return unwinds proportionally and leaves the rest sold; a full return returns the full tax and nets the pair to zero gross; a partial return returns only the proportional tax; a discounted line returns what was paid rather than list; a reversal materializes no subscription; the return's entry balances on its own; returning more than was bought is refused with the remaining quantity stated; two partial returns may not exceed the original between them; and a reversal pointing at a line for a different product is refused.
